business_scope.primary_industry_name: Stock Photography Marketplace and Generative Visual Assets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary state; single national company registry and no sub-state incorporation distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with direct application of EU Regulations and EU-Directive-transposed national law
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–U.S. Double Taxation Agreement (1996, amended by 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (current consolidated treaty, as amended and in force)
Luxembourg–Singapore Double Taxation Agreement (current in-force treaty)
EU–Singapore Free Trade Agreement (in force since 21 November 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (governing SCSp without legal personality); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the operationalisation of the UBO Register; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF circulars on conduct-of-business rules; EU Regulation 2015/849 (4AMLD) and EU Directive 2018/843 (5AMLD) transposition.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport / national identity card of each natural-person UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / notary in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if origin is an Apostille Convention party; elsewhere Consular Legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / registration extract and corporate ownership chart for each corporate partner or indirect shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant company registry in the corporate UBO's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or alternative Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised power of attorney / board resolution authorising the Luxembourg incorporation agent and local legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or corporate board/body in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; original signature pages to be sighted by Luxembourg counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified sworn-translation into French, German or Luxembourgish of all foreign constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traducteur agréé) in Luxembourg or licence-holder in the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the translator's/certifying authority's signature, or consular authentication

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory anti-money-laundering identity verification, PEP and sanctions screening on every UBO, general partner, manager and beneficial signatory before RCS filing. Screening is performed against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions regimes, OFAC SDN List (when USD payment rails are used), and the CSSF's national high-risk third-country lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, high-risk third countries and complex ownership structures; source-of-funds documentation must be collected for any PEP or sanctioned-jurisdiction nexus. Suspicious transaction reports are filed with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) under Article 5 of the 2004 AML/CFT Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — www.lbr.lu / RCS electronic filing and name reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Legal names must use Latin-alphabet characters; French, German, Luxembourgish and English names are accepted. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters in the RCS file and a certified translation retained. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and the legal-form suffix 'Société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp' must appear in the registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: LUXEMBOURG (or LETZEBUERG) when suggesting public/state entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name may be extended once for an additional 90 days before expiration. If the RCS rejects the name, the applicant may, within one month of receipt of the rejection, file an internal review request with the RCS; if refusal is maintained, an appeal may be taken to the Luxembourg Tribunal de l'Entreprise (commercial chamber) within one month of notification. The proposed name remains blocked during appeal; a materially different name can be re-filed immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A mere letterbox or PO Box is not permissible. A registered office in Luxembourg can be supplied by a CSSF-supervised licensed domiciliation service provider. This is acceptable for an SCSp operating an online stock-photo/AI marketplace with no physical employees, as long as the domiciliation agent can accept service of process, maintain corporate files, and provide correspondence handling.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 2–5% probability of an unannounced inspection in the first year for this non-licensed, low-risk segment. The probability rises to approximately 15–20% if a UBO or manager is a PEP, is resident in a high-risk third country, or if RCS/UBO discrepancies are identified. Inspections may be conducted by the RCS, CSSF, tax authorities (ACD) or the State Prosecutor.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 319-1 to 319-7 (special limited partnership – SCSp), and Articles 1-20 (general partnership provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCSL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration of an SCSp (contrat de société / partnership agreement) filed via the MyGuichet portal; the partnership becomes validly constituted upon entry in the RCSL.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely governs capital contributions, including in-cash or in-kind, and no escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The general partner, acting as the board of managers of the Luxembourg SCSp, hereby resolves: (1) That the limited partnership agreement presented to this board be approved and adopted as governing instrument; (2) That the initial capital contributions be accepted and that the registration be filed with the RCSL; (3) That the registered office be established at 1, Rue Robert Stümper, L-2557 Luxembourg; (4) That [Full Name] be appointed managing partner with exclusive authority to file the registration, open bank accounts, appoint service providers, and sign regulatory declarations; (5) That all actions already taken in connection with these matters are ratified. Done and signed by the general partner upon the date below.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional) and initial partners; subsequent filing with RCSL via MyGuichet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in accordance with Articles 319-1 to 319-7 of the Law of 10 August 1915. Define the identity of the general partner and limited partners, capital contributions, profit/loss allocation, management powers, and termination rules. Execute the agreement by all partners before a notary if real property is contributed; otherwise a private deed suffices. Obtain certified copies and authenticated IDs.
required_dossiers: Passport copies or national ID cards of all partners
Proof of residential address for each partner
Certified bank references or proof of contribution capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary queries the draft, amend deficient clauses, re-execute signatures, and resubmit; no penalty is incurred provided correction occurs before the formal RCSL filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for Registration with the RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) through the MyGuichet portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application electronically, attaching the executed partnership agreement and legalisation evidence. Complete the standard company particulars form and declare the registered office in Luxembourg. Pay the filing fee through the portal after preliminary validation. Retain the submission acknowledgement containing the file reference.
required_dossiers: Notarised or signed partnership agreement (as applicable)
Identification documents of the general partner and managers
Consent of the owner for use of registered office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the RCSL rectification request within 15 days by uploading corrected documents through MyGuichet; if final rejection occurs, re-file after curing all noted defects, preserving any appeal rights under Luxembourg administrative law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice and Extraction of RCSL Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCSL registers the SCSp, the registry automatically arranges publication of a legal notice in the RESA. Monitor the RESA website for the publication, verify the accuracy of all data, and download the official RCSL extract and certificate of incorporation / registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication contains errors, file a written rectification request with the RCSL accompanied by the correct data and the original extract; corrections are processed without retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the mandatory VAT registration application with the AEDT before engaging in taxable activities. Describe the stock photography marketplace and AI-generated visual assets as electronic services. Complete the identification process to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number and business identification number.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the managing partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests clarification on the place of supply of digital services, submit a technical explanation of the platform's infrastructure and customer base; amendment may be made without fiscal penalties if filed in good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Social Security Setup (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CNSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional bank account in the SCSp's name by presenting the RCSL certificate and partnership agreement. If the company intends to hire employees, register the employer with the CNSS within 8 days of hiring. Establish the contractual relationship and execute bank mandates as per the partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: Identification and passport of the managing partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced KYC documentation, provide an organisational chart and source of funds declarations. For CNSS late registration, submit a formal justification and request retroactive registration to avoid late-payment penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial manufacturing activity is performed; the digital stock photography marketplace falls outside the scope of industrial licensing under the Ministry of the Economy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no statutory operating or manufacturing permit applies to an online marketplace for stock photographs and generative visual assets.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – fully digital service activity, no physical installation, construction, emission source or discharge point; no EIA notification or registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation; the only environmental requirement is compliance with general waste segregation and electronic equipment disposal obligations under the Luxembourg Waste Law if office hardware is used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – the SCSp has no physical premises requiring fire safety certification or structural load inspection. If a future office is established, the premises must comply with the general work safety and accessibility standards of the Labour Code; an initial workplace declaration (for social security and labour inspection purposes) must be filed through the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; centralized e-administration portal: MyGuichet.lu and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the SCSp by notarial or private deed and file with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) platform; obtain the sole national registration number (numéro d'identification / matricule) assigned upon RCS filing, which serves as the direct-tax reference; submit VAT registration to the AEDT on Form 640 before commencing activity, obtaining the Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits); non-resident partners are not separately registered unless directly taxable in Luxembourg; all filings and registry communications are executed via MyGuichet.lu with notarized or legalized supporting documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election under Article 4(2) of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) for the SCSp to be taxed as a body corporate (opaque taxation) where it carries on a commercial activity and all partners are subject to corporate income tax; optional waiver of the VAT small-business exemption; US check-the-box election remains available for eligible transparent SCSp entities for US federal income tax; ATAD and hybrid-mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2018) constrain divergent tax classifications in cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover excluding VAT (small-business franchise exemption, optional and waivable); non-established foreign suppliers have a zero threshold and must register immediately; intra-Community distance sales threshold EUR 10,000 per calendar year.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, or digital stamping regime in Luxembourg; mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL (PEPPOL BIS 3.0/UBL 2.1 or CII) since October 2016; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and is expected to become mandatory only under the EU ViDA framework (target horizon 2030-2035).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods qualify for the mandatory 0% rate where dispatch or transport begins in Luxembourg and terminates outside the EU (Article 51 of the Luxembourg VAT Law); supplies of digital stock-photo licensing to non-EU business customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules (Article 17 VAT Law for B2B and Article 18 for B2C digital services); payment-processing via Stripe or PayPal does not alter the place-of-supply test; documentary proof of export or of the customer's foreign establishment must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (single administrative declaration)
Export customs approval or electronic proof of export (EX/PBN record)
Commercial invoice with full buyer and consignee details
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch outside the EU
Proof of payment (bank transfer or inward remittance certificate)
Customer contract or license deed confirming the place of establishment
Intra-Community supply evidence where stock is transported to another EU Member State (customer VAT ID and recapitulative statement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess and claw back incorrectly claimed zero-rated exports for up to five years, or up to ten years in cases of fraud; unpaid VAT carries default interest of 0.8% per month; administrative fines under Article 96 of the Luxembourg VAT Law reach EUR 5,000 per offence; criminal tax evasion penalties under the General Tax Law reach EUR 50,000, and fraudulent VAT schemes may trigger sanctions under the Criminal Code with joint and several liability of the SCSp general partner and any appointed tax representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the Luxembourg monetary authority and integrated Eurosystem member. Prudential and AML/CFT supervision of all banks, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, and CSSF Circular 20/725. The BCL is the competent authority for balance-of-payments statistical reporting and systemic payment-systems oversight; together they form the dual control regime governing cross-border banking, FX, and clearing in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility by virtue of Eurozone membership and Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). There are no exchange controls, no prior-authorisation requirements, no quantitative limits, and no administrative hurdles on the repatriation of profits, dividends, royalties, interest, or capital proceeds for residents or non-residents. A 100% foreign-owned special limited partnership (SCSp) may freely receive equity contributions and remit royalty, licence, and commission income to any jurisdiction, subject only to: (i) Luxembourg withholding-tax law and applicable double-tax treaties; (ii) DAC6/ATAD transparency rules; and (iii) the bank's internal AML/CFT due-diligence checks. The practical friction points are compliance documentation and tax substance, not convertibility law. The ECB's standing foreign-exchange regulations permit the euro to be freely traded and hedged, including forwards, swaps, and options with EU-authorised counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no cadenced repatriation deadline, and no obligation to centralise foreign-exchange revenue with the BCL or any Luxembourg bank. Receipts from the export of digital stock-photo licences and generative visual-asset royalties, whether collected in USD, GBP, EUR, or other currencies, may be retained in foreign currency in Luxembourg accounts or converted at the SCSp's discretion. The only regulatory incidentals are: (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, which is normally intermediated by the executing credit institution and uses purpose codes for each cross-border flow; and (ii) EU Regulation 2021/1230 on cross-border payments, which requires equal EUR/non-EUR pricing and full transparency on conversion charges when the SCSp receives remittances via SEPA or equivalent systems. Professional practice is to record each inbound royalty wire with the appropriate BCL purpose code and to maintain the settlement statements of the payment facilitator for the bank's periodic review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with SWIFT GPI and FX Forward access

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus Capital Escrow Account for fund-vehicle structures
Operational Account and Treasury Sub-Accounts with securities/FX collateral capability
Operational Account with SEPA Instant, Direct Debit, and automated FX conversion modules
Operational Account with global SWIFT connectivity and e-Banking host-to-host reporting
Capital Escrow / Depository Account for SCSp fund-vehicle structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for operational collection, LOW for treasury and capital-escrow functions. Luxembourg recognises payment institutions and electronic money institutions under the Law of 10 November 2009 (transposing PSD2) and the CSSF regulatory perimeter. Viable local EMIs/PSPs for a stock-photo marketplace include Stripe (Stripe Payments Luxembourg S.A., CSSF-authorised as a payment institution), PayPal Luxembourg S.à r.l. (electronic money institution), and Mangopay S.A. (Luxembourg-incorporated EMI specialised in marketplace payouts). EU-passported EMIs such as Airwallex, Wise, or Revolut may operate in Luxembourg under freedom-of-services notification to the CSSF, but they cannot be used as the sole depository of the SCSp's capital, because the legal architecture of an SCSp capital account requires a credit institution for depositary/escrow safety and for the BCL statistical chain. The correct treasury posture is: EMIs/PSPs are used for merchant-side collection and sub-merchant payouts; a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank is the exclusive holder of the operating treasury and escrow balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote opening is possible but de facto rare for a first-time non-resident SCSp. Under CSSF Circular 20/725, remote onboarding must use certified video-identification with qualified electronic-signature mechanisms and register an audit trail; in practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one initial physical or video-conference interview with the general partner's authorised signatory and the natural-person beneficial owners exceeding 25%. For a US-managed SCSp, banks customarily accept a physical interview at a Luxembourg desk, an attested copy of the passport, and an apostilled certificate of incumbency from the US parent. Directors who cannot attend in person must produce a Luxembourg-notarised power of attorney and original bank references from their home jurisdiction; pure 'correspondence-only' opening without interview is rejected for a newly registered SCSp with no prior banking history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp flagged as a tax-transparent special-purpose 'shell': the structure has no employees, no material local premises, and the bank doubts legal personality and economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS Luxembourg registration extract (extrait du registre de commerce et des sociétés), notarised Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA), certificate of active status from the Luxembourg beneficial-owner register, a Luxembourg counsel legal opinion confirming the SCSp's legal personality and the general partner's authority, plus a substance file comprising the registered-office lease, domain-name/IP registration certificates, board minutes, stage-gated business plan, and commercial contracts evidencing the operating stock-photo and AI-licensing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the UBO chain: an indirect ownership structure through a US LP or non-EU holding vehicle triggers enhanced due diligence and a presumption of structured layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain chart down to the ultimate natural persons, RBE extract of the SCSp under the Law of 13 January 2019, certificate of good standing and register extracts of every intermediate entity (Delaware/Florida/Nevada as applicable), incumbency and register-of-directors certificates, passport copies of each >25% natural person, and source-of-wealth statements supported by bank references and tax returns of the controlling individuals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated high-volume micro-payment stream: repeated Stripe/PayPal settlements with low individual ticket values are treated as potential SMS/red-flag activity masking third-party funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform agreements (stock marketplace and generative model distribution agreements), actual Stripe/PayPal periodic settlement statements reconciled to the bank statements, a transaction-log export mapping each settlement to customer licences, commission and fee schedules, a chart of accounts certified by a Luxembourg accountant identifying ISIC 7420 revenue, and a written compliance certificate from the payment facilitator listing all merchant identifiers and confirming no pass-through of third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-country counterparty exposure: receipts from US and APAC clients, together with discretionary cloud and AI-compute costs, raise sanctions-screening and trade-sanctions risk alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU sanctions screening results for all known counterparties and ultimate clients, completed KYB questionnaires from each distribution platform, contractual clauses prohibiting transacting with blocked persons, a sanctions-compliance procedure document, full beneficial-owner declarations of all licensing counterparties, and a sworn attestation that no funds originate from virtual-asset or non-bank unregulated channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-contribution disproportionality: an early-stage AI company injecting large contributed capital without a commensurate EBITDA or payroll history is reviewed as potential liability-factoring or ALD-risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed pro-forma cash-flow model linking injected capital to cloud compute, content acquisition, and international marketing expenses; capital-call notices issued in conformity with the LPA; bank statements demonstrating the wire trail from the investing partners; the cap-table software export of all equity issuances; valuation memorandum for the generative visual-asset portfolio; and source-of-funds certificates of the subscribing partners backed by their home-bank professional references.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign investor originates a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the SCSp's operational account at a Luxembourg Tier-1 bank, using the SCSp's IBAN and its LEI code in field 72. The remittance information field must state the purpose as 'Capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp' and reference the specific capital-call notice. For balance-of-payments statistical coding, the bank records the flow as a direct-investment equity transaction in the BCL external-statistics classification; the investor's bank may additionally require the Luxembourg LPA, the certificate of registration, and a funds-identification letter. If the investment is funded via a US entity, the corridor wire from the US correspondent bank to the Luxembourg BIC must carry a full legal name of the SCSp and the reference 'SCSP_LU SCI IP Contribution — no contravention of OFAC'. Private-equity style capital calls should be pre-announced to the Luxembourg bank to avoid a false positive in automatic transaction monitoring. The bank will also request a signed 'Declaration of Source of Funds' and confirmation that the contribution is not a repayable loan; if the contribution is temporarily parked in a capital-escrow account, the LPA and the sponsor's instruction letter must explicitly authorise the use of that account before treasury deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for euro payments within the EU — used for contributor royalty payouts, cloud-provider invoices, and administrative fees; SEPA Instant is recommended for low-value monthly content-contributor settlements; (ii) SWIFT MT103 with SWIFT GPI tracking for non-EU disbursements (US contributors, APAC distribution partners, licensing agents) — each MT103 must include the payment purpose code (e.g., 'Royalties and licence fees' under the BCL statistical nomenclature), the underlying invoice reference, and any required withholding-tax certification; (iii) commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit (MT700/MT760) are not material to stock-photo royalty flows and should be reserved for large content-library or artwork acquisitions, where a confirmed irrevocable LC at a Luxembourg bank (or a standby LC guaranteeing the performance of the SCSp's licensor) provides settlement assurance; and (iv) card-network settlement rails (Visa/Mastercard) via Stripe and PayPal, which settle funds in bulk to the Luxembourg account after acquiring and clearing cycles. For recurring USD settlement, the SCSp should establish a multi-currency account with automatic FX-sweep instructions so that USD collector balances convert to EUR at a pre-agreed daily rate; the bank sweeps balances via an internal FX conversion without a separate SWIFT wire, reducing costs and audit fatigue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (deliverable) in EUR/USD and EUR/GBP with tenors up to 12 months under a standard international FX Master Agreement or ISDA 2002 Master Agreement — the primary instrument to lock conversion on expected quarterly USD/GBP settlement flows from stock-photo and licensing platforms
FX Swaps (spot-forward combination) for liquidity bridging when the SCSp holds USD inflows but must pay EUR-denominated AI-compute and contributor costs
Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD) for any material acquisition debt or significant treasury-exposure periods exceeding 12 months, requiring full ISDA/CSA documentation and bank credit approval
European-style FX Options (vanilla calls and puts) on EUR/USD, purchased (not written) to protect royalty-convertibility budgets while preserving upside in a strengthening EUR

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are permitted in Luxembourg for exotic or illiquid currency pairs (e.g., certain APAC and EMEA currencies) if the counterparty is an EU-authorised credit institution or a licensed broker-dealer, but NDFs are not necessary or recommended for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, which are fully deliverable in the liquid euro FX market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for late or missing filing; possible administrative removal from the RCS; RCS good-standing certificate may be withheld

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – UBO Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change; no separate annual filing required if data remains unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 for non-disclosure or inaccurate data; criminal penalties may apply for intentional violations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership tax information return (declaration fiscale for a transparent entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June following the tax year; an extension to 30 September may be granted for online filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest, fine up to EUR 4,000, and possibility of assessment based on the tax administration's estimation

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SCSp exceeds any two of the following in the fiscal year: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4,400,000, net turnover exceeding EUR 8,800,000, or average staff exceeding 50; audit may also be triggered by the partnership agreement or by a partner request
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP is the default framework; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be applied if elected and properly disclosed

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO re-filing applies if no change occurs; the general partner must conduct an annual internal review of UBO accuracy and confirm the register upon RCS request. Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of occurrence, together with supporting documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (partners – holdings and transfers)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the SCSp level (fiscally transparent partnership). Partners are taxed on their allocated share: a Luxembourg-resident corporate partner faces an aggregate CIT headline rate of approx. 24.94% (CIT 17.00% + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19% + communal business tax ~6.75% in Luxembourg City).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box (Art. 50bis LIR): 80% exclusion of qualifying net IP income, yielding an effective rate of approx. 5% (20% x 24.94%) on qualifying royalties from proprietary AI-generation software and protected visual-asset licences. Participation exemption (Art. 166 LIR) for qualifying capital gains. Notional interest deduction (Art. 168bis LIR) on qualifying new equity increases. No net wealth tax on the transparent SCSp itself. Since 1 Jan 2024, dividend exemption-at-source applies to qualifying 10%/12-month corporate shareholders.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (Art. 114 LIR; no statutory expiry). Losses of the transparent SCSp flow through to partners and are deductible at partner level subject to the AED's change-of-ownership/utilization controls; temporary one-year carry-back applied only for COVID-19 years (2020-2021).
